'''Kasturi Lal Chopra''' (31 July 1933 – 18 May 2021) was an Indian [[Materials physics|materials physicist]] and a director of the [[Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur]].<ref name="Indian fellow">{{cite web | url=http://insaindia.res.in/detail.php?id=N78-0163 | title=Indian fellow | publisher=Indian National Science Academy | date=2016 | access-date=27 August 2016}}</ref> He was the founder of the ''Thin Film Laboratory'' at [[Indian Institute of Technology, Delhi]] and the ''Microscience Laboratory'' at IIT, Kharagpur and held several US and Indian patents for his research findings.<ref name="Top scientists misuse power, funds">{{cite web | url=https://www.downtoearth.org.in/interviews/top-scientists-misuse-power-funds-48988 | title=Top scientists misuse power, funds | publisher=Down to Earth | date=31 March 2015 | access-date=27 August 2016}}</ref> Author of a number of books on [[thin film]] technology,<ref name="Listing on National Library of Australia">{{cite web | url=http://trove.nla.gov.au/result?q=creator%3A%22Chopra%2C+Kasturi+L.%2C+1933-%22 | title=Listing on National Library of Australia | publisher=National Library of Australia | date=2016 | access-date=27 August 2016}}</ref> he was a recipient of [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]], the highest Indian award in the science and technology categories.<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/Detail.aspx?AID=436 | title=Brief Profile of the Awardee | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research | date=2016 | access-date=27 August 2016}}</ref> The Government of India awarded him the fourth highest civilian honour of the [[Padma Shri]], in 2008, for his contributions to science and engineering.<ref name="Padma Awards">{{cite web|url=http://mha.nic.in/sites/upload_files/mha/files/LST-PDAWD-2013.pdf |title=Padma Awards |publisher=Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India |date=2013 |access-date=20 August 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151015193758/http://mha.nic.in/sites/upload_files/mha/files/LST-PDAWD-2013.pdf |archive-date=15 October 2015 }}</ref>

== Biography ==
[[File:IIT Kharagpur Main Building.JPG|thumb|235px|Institute Main Building, IIT Kharagpur]]
K. L. Chopra was born on 31 July 1933 at Chahal Kalan in the [[Gujranwala District]] of [[Punjab Province (British India)|British Punjab Province]] to Jagat Ram and Chanan Devi Chopra. He studied science at the [[University of Delhi]] from which he graduated with honors in physics in 1952, and followed it up with a master's degree from the same university in 1954.<ref name="Biodata on Indian Institute of Technology, Delhi">{{cite web | url=http://tfl.iitd.ac.in/Chop-Bio-1.pdf | title=Biodata on Indian Institute of Technology, Delhi | publisher=Indian Institute of Technology, Delhi | date=2016 | access-date=27 August 2016 | archive-date=28 August 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160828222048/http://tfl.iitd.ac.in/Chop-Bio-1.pdf | url-status=dead }}</ref> He pursued his doctoral studies at the [[University of British Columbia]] on a fellowship and secured his PhD in ''low temperature physics'' in 1957.<ref name="Indian fellow" /> Continuing his stay in North America, he served as a defence research fellow at the [[Royal Military College of Canada]] (1957–59) and as a staff scientist at Philco-Ford Scientific Laboratory (1962–64) and Ledgemont Laboratory of Kennecott Copper Corporation (1964–70), during which time he also took up academic positions as an adjunct professor at [[Northeastern University]] and as a visiting professor at [[Cornell University]]. Concurrently, he served as a consultant to IBM, Westinghouse and ARCO and had a short stint at [[Fritz Haber Institute of the Max Planck Society]], Berlin (1959–62) in between, as their fellow. Returning to India, he was appointed as a senior professor of [[solid state physics]] at the [[Indian Institute of Technology, Delhi]] in 1970 where he served till 1987, holding positions such as that of the Head of Department of Physics (1970–73), Dean of the Faculty of Science (1973–74), Chair and Dean Industrial Research and Development (1975–76), Dean of the Post Graduate Studies and Research (1976–79), Head of the Centre for Energy Studies (1983–85), Senior Professor of Physics and Head of the ''Thin Film Solid State Technology Laboratory'' and the Dean of Industrial Research and Development (1985–87) till his superannuation in 1987.<ref name="Biodata on Indian Institute of Technology, Delhi" />

Chopra was invited to head the [[Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur]] in 1987 and worked there till 1997 as the Director of the Institution when he was appointed as the Chair Professor of Renewable Energy at Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency (IREDA), a post he held till 2000.<ref name="Indian fellow" /> After retiring from active service in 2000, he continues his association with many scientific and academic institutions and chairs HDF School of Management, Bhubaneswar and Budge Budge Institute of Technology, Kolkata while holding the distinguished chair professorship of [[Indian Institute of Engineering Science and Technology, Shibpur]] (formerly known as BESU, Kolkata).<ref name="Biodata on Indian Institute of Technology, Delhi" /> He was also an adviser to the ''Thin Film Laboratory'' of IIT, Delhi, and [[Jaypee University of Engineering and Technology]], Madhya Pradesh. He was the founder member of the Society for Scientific Values, an organization serving as a watchdog for promoting integrity and ethics in scientific pursuit, and served as its president and then patron until his death.<ref name="Executive Council">{{cite web | url=http://www.scientificvalues.org/exec.html | title=Executive Council | publisher=Society for Scientific Values | date=2016 | access-date=27 August 2016}}</ref> He served as the vice president of the Materials Research Society of India and was a life member of the society.<ref name="Life Members">{{cite web | url=http://www.mrsi.org.in/members-category.php | title=Life Members | publisher=Materials Research Society of India | date=2016 | access-date=27 August 2016}}</ref> He was also a former member of the council of the [[Indian National Science Academy]] (1988–90) and served as an honorary professor at [[King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals]], Saudi Arabia, IIT Delhi, IIEST Shibpur and [[Indian Institute of Technology Bhubaneswar]].<ref name="Biodata on Indian Institute of Technology, Delhi" />

Chopra died following an infection with [[COVID-19]] on 19 May 2021, at the age of 87. He and his wife also had bilateral knee [[osteoarthritis]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Padma Shri Prof. Kasturi Lal Chopra, FNA (31st July 1932 – 19th May 2021) passes away |url=https://dst.gov.in/sites/default/files/Obituary%20Padma%20Shri%20Prof%20K%20L%20Chopra.pdf |website=dst.gov.in |access-date=18 September 2024}}</ref>

== Legacy ==
Working on [[thin films]] and [[nanomatter]], Chopra did pioneering studies through which he established ''specular scattering of electrons in epitaxial metal films'', discovered ''field induced nucleation and growth process'' as well as ''giant photocontraction effect in amorphous chalcogenide films'', developed ''semiconducting metallopolymer films'' and proposed new process protocols for low dimensional nanomaterials and high temperature superconductors.<ref name="Indian fellow" /> He published his findings through more than 430 research articles and ten books, which include ''Thin film phenomena'',<ref name="Thin film phenomena">{{cite book | title=Thin film phenomena | publisher=McGraw-Hill | author=Kasturi L Chopra | year=1969 | pages=864 | oclc=499963884}}</ref> ''Thin Film Solar Cells'',<ref name="Thin Film Solar Cells">{{cite book | title=Thin Film Solar Cells | publisher=Springer Science+Business Media | author=Kasturi Lal Chopra, Suhit Ranjan Das | year=1983 | isbn=978-1-4899-0420-1| doi=10.1007/978-1-4899-0418-8 }}</ref> ''Thin Film Device Applications''<ref name="Thin Film Device Applications">{{cite book | title=Thin Film Device Applications | publisher=Springer | author=Kasturi Lal Chopra | year=1983 | isbn=9780306412974}}</ref> and ''Vacuum Science and Technology''.<ref name="RaoGosh1998">{{cite book|author1=Dr. V.V. Rao|author2=Dr. T.B. Gosh|author3=Dr. K.L. Chopra|title=Vacuum Science and Technology|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ys7yQ1lpVdUC|date=17 October 1998|publisher=Allied Publishers|isbn=978-81-7023-763-1}}</ref> He also edited two books, ''Thin Film Technology and Applications: International Workshop, New Delhi, Nov. 1984, Proceedings''<ref name="ChopraMalhotra1985">{{cite book|author1=K.L. Chopra|author2=L.K. Malhotra, Indian Institute of Technology. Thin Film Laboratory-Committee on Science and Technology in Developing Countries|title=Thin Film Technology and Applications: International Workshop, New Delhi, Nov. 1984, Proceedings|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gen7nAEACAAJ|year=1985|publisher=Tata McGraw-Hill|isbn=9780074515693}}</ref> and ''Thin Films 7: Proceedings of the 7th International Conference on Thin Films, New Delhi, India, December 7–11, 1987''.<ref name="Chopra1988">{{cite book|author=Kasturi L. Chopra|title=Thin Films 7: Proceedings of the 7th International Conference on Thin Films, New Delhi, India, December 7-11, 1987|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XvB3QAAACAAJ|year=1988|publisher=Elsevier Applied Science|isbn=978-1-85166-980-6}}</ref> He held six US patents and eight of his know-hows are in use with Indian industries. Besides, he mentored 100 MTech and 60 PhD students in their researches and served as a member of the editorial boards of many journals. It was during his tenure as the head of the institution, the ''Thin Film Laboratory'' of IIT Delhi<ref name="Padma Shri Prof. Kasturi Lal Chopra ">{{cite web | url=http://tfl.iitd.ac.in/ | title=Padma Shri Prof. Kasturi Lal Chopra | publisher=Thin Film Laboratory | date=2016 | access-date=27 August 2016}}</ref> and ''Microscience Laboratory'' of IIT Kharagpur were established.<ref name="Indian fellow" />

== Awards and honors ==
During his stay in the US, Chopra received four patent awards from Kennecott Copper Corporation between 1966 and 1970.<ref name="Biodata on Indian Institute of Technology, Delhi" /> The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]] awarded him [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]], the highest Indian award in the science and engineering categories, in 1975.<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee" /> He received [[Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce & Industry|FICCI]] Award in 1983 and two more awards in 1989, Bhabha Award of the [[University Grants Commission (India)|University Grants Commission]] and [[Om Prakash Bhasin Award]].<ref name="Om Prakash Bhasin Awards">{{cite web | url=https://www.opbfawards.com/engineering.html | title=Om Prakash Bhasin Awards | publisher=Shri Om Prakash Bhasin Foundation | date=2016 | access-date=27 August 2016}}</ref> The Indian Vacuum Society awarded him Distinguished Vacuum Scientist Award in 1994, and the next year, he received the Distinguished Material Scientist Award of the Materials Research Society of India, the highest award of the society.<ref name="Distinguished Materials Scientist of the year award">{{cite web | url=http://www.mrsi.org.in/awardshonours.php | title=Distinguished Materials Scientist of the year award | publisher=Materials Research Society of India | date=2016 | access-date=27 August 2016}}</ref> The [[Indian National Science Academy]] awarded him the Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis Medal in 1996 and the Aryabhata Medal in 2004.<ref name="Recipients of Medals/Lectures Awards">{{cite web | url=http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#abs | title=Recipients of Medals/Lectures Awards | publisher=Indian National Science Academy | date=2016 | access-date=27 August 2016 | archive-date=16 September 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160916233840/http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#abs | url-status=dead }}</ref> In between, he received two awards, the Lifetime Achievement Award of the Solar Energy Society of India and ISI Citation Laureate Award.<ref name="Biodata on Indian Institute of Technology, Delhi" /> The Government of India included him in the [[Indian honours system|Republic Day honors]] list for the civilian honor of the [[Padma Shri]] in 2008 and he received the Distinguished Engineering Educator Award of the Indian Society of Mechanical Engineers, the same year.<ref name="Biodata on Indian Institute of Technology, Delhi" /> He is also a recipient of the Freedom of the Institute Award of the IIIT Delhi and Distinguished Academician Award of [[Indian Institute of Technology Patna]].<ref name="Indian fellow" />

The [[Indian National Science Academy]] elected Chopra as their fellow in 1978 and the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]]<ref name="Fellow Profile">{{cite web | url=http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Chopra,_Prof._Kasturi_Lal | title=Fellow Profile | publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences | date=2016 | access-date=27 August 2016}}</ref> and the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]] followed suit in 1980 and 1988 respectively.<ref name="NASI fellows">{{cite web|url=http://www.nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=C |title=NASI fellows |publisher=National Academy of Sciences, India |date=2016 |access-date=27 August 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160315111634/http://nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=C |archive-date=15 March 2016 }}</ref> He was also an elected fellow of the [[Indian National Academy of Engineering]],<ref name="INAE fellows">{{cite web | url=http://inae.in/search-of-fellows/ | title=INAE fellows | publisher=Indian Academy of Engineering | date=2016 | access-date=27 August 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150403030936/http://inae.in/search-of-fellows/ | archive-date=3 April 2015 | url-status=dead }}</ref> Asian Pacific Society for Materials Research and the [[American Physical Society]] and an honorary fellow of Punjab Academy of Sciences.<ref name="List Of Honorary Fellows">{{cite web | url=http://paspatiala.com/honorary.html | title=List Of Honorary Fellows | publisher=Punjab Academy of Sciences | date=2016 | access-date=27 August 2016 }}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> [[Uttar Pradesh Technical University]] conferred the degree of Doctor of Science ([[honoris causa]]) on him in 2006, followed by the Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur in 2010.<ref name="Institute Lecture">{{cite web | url=https://www.iitk.ac.in/olddord/institutelecture_2008.pdf | title=Institute Lecture | publisher=Indian Institute of Technology, Kanpur | date=2016 | access-date=27 August 2016}}</ref> He delivered several award orations and keynote addresses including K. S. Krishnan Memorial Award Lecture of the Indian National Science Academy (1992),<ref name="Recipients of Medals/Lectures Awards" /> Biren Roy Memorial Lecture Award (1997), Institute Lecture on ''Ethical Values in Science and Technology'' of the Indian Institute of Technology, Kanpur (2008) and D. S. Kothari Memorial Oration Award of the [[Defence Laboratory, Jodhpur]] (2009).<ref name="Institute Lecture" />
